research_note: SWE-CoWork preprint submitted November 15, 2026. 101 assignments from real code repositories evaluated inside simulated engineering organizations; 11 models evaluated. Two leading models completed fewer than 8% of assignments. Not a general claim about all coding agents or engineering work.

segments.title: AI CAN CODE. BUT CAN IT FINISH?
segments.caption: A new benchmark tests full task delivery.
segments.speech: Code Crew! AI can write code. But can it actually finish a software engineer's job?

segments.title: 101 REAL REPOSITORIES
segments.caption: SWE-CoWork: simulated engineering workplaces.
segments.speech: Researchers created SWE-CoWork: one hundred and one development assignments using real code repositories, inside simulated engineering teams.

segments.title: UNDER 8% COMPLETE
segments.caption: Two leading models; full-assignment completion.
segments.speech: Eleven AI models were tested. Even the two leading models fully completed fewer than eight percent of assignments!

segments.title: CODING ISN'T DELIVERY
segments.caption: Partial test success is not full delivery.
segments.speech: They could pass many individual tests. But gathering requirements, collaborating, and shipping the whole task? Much harder!

segments.title: DEVELOPERS STILL MATTER
segments.caption: One benchmark, not every coding task.
segments.speech: This is one research benchmark, not a verdict on every AI tool. So, will agents replace developers or become their best teammates? Tell us below, and follow Learn With Obscure!
